title: Historical density-shift fits do not determine the projected CalCOFI hypoxia date under a response that can weaken
abstract: We test whether the historical North Pacific density-shift law determines the projected date of oxygen below 60 micromol/kg off California. The frozen reference profile needs a shift of 0.2373 kg/m3. The largest finite historical upper limit in 116 selected summary rows is 0.165. All 65 first crossings across the source model cases occur beyond this range. We derive sharp conditional bounds when the transfer response slope can stay between zero and one. Smooth laws that exactly preserve the historical response can prevent every crossing. A tail scale of 0.05 kg/m3 gives an oxygen floor of 66.00. A scale of 0.10 delays the SSP2-4.5 observed-start median crossing from 2062 to 2079. The original law is the low-oxygen endpoint of the bounded-slope family. This is an identification result, not a new forecast or evidence that the ocean response will weaken. Raw hydrography, process budgets and future solubility changes are not tested. Code, frozen aggregate inputs, source hashes, numerical results and checked regeneration are included.

display.caption: Response laws agree through the protected historical shift range but give different future oxygen. The right panel uses SSP2-4.5 and the observed-start variant.
